core_obligations: Deduce assertion (2) from assertion (1) and the converse criterion of the previous lemma (proof lines 8875-8877).
Reduce assertion (1) formally to the case of a morphism X_A -> Spec(A) over a valuation ring, using base change stability (proof lines 8878-8895).
Show that x : Spec(K) -> X is quasi-compact from quasi-separatedness and quasi-compactness, so that |f|(closure of the image of x) is closed in Spec(A) (proof lines 8898-8910).
Since that closed image contains the generic point, find a point x' in the closure of x mapping to the closed point of Spec(A) (proof lines 8911-8913).
Apply the reaching-points lemma to obtain the valuation ring extension A' of A and the commutative diagram whose closed point maps to x', and conclude that A' dominates A (proof lines 8914-8924).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its two assertions: a quasi-separated universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion, and for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated universal closedness is equivalent to that criterion (source lines 8861-8872). The second assertion follows by combining the first with the converse criterion. The first is the substantive direction and is proved by a point-set argument: after a formal reduction to a base change X_A -> Spec(A) for a valuation ring A with fraction field K, one uses that the quasi-separatedness of f makes the morphism x : Spec(K) -> X quasi-compact, hence |f|(closure of {x}) is closed in Spec(A) because f is universally closed, so it contains the closed point and there is a point x' in the closure of x mapping to it; a reaching-points lemma then produces the extension A' of A and the required commutative diagram.
